summary: Quebec City is a charming European-inspired destination nestled along the St. Lawrence River, featuring cobblestone streets, historic architecture, and vibrant French-Canadian culture. With world-class cuisine, stunning natural landscapes, and rich heritage sites, it offers an enchanting escape that feels worlds away despite its North American location. The city transforms dramatically with seasons, making it a photographer's paradise year-round.

restaurants.name: Cactus Club
restaurants.description: Casual taqueria in the Saint-Roch neighborhood serving authentic Mexican street food and fresh seafood tacos. A local favorite known for generous portions and vibrant atmosphere.

restaurants.name: L'Affaire Est Ketchup
restaurants.description: Cozy neighborhood bistro specializing in Quebec comfort food with a modern twist. Features seasonal ingredients and traditional poutine elevated with gourmet toppings.

restaurants.name: Panache
restaurants.description: Located in the historic Auberge Saint-Antoine, this upscale restaurant offers contemporary French cuisine with local influences. Elegant ambiance perfect for special occasions with views of the St. Lawrence River.

restaurants.name: Rue Saint-Paul Brasserie
restaurants.description: Traditional French brasserie in Old Quebec serving classic dishes like coq au vin and beef bourguignon. Charming interior with vintage bistro decor creates authentic Parisian atmosphere.
restaurants.mustTry: Coq au vin with red wine reduction

restaurants.name: Portobello Market
restaurants.description: Casual market-style eatery featuring fresh seasonal produce, local cheeses, and prepared foods. Great for quick, affordable meals with authentic Quebec products.
restaurants.mustTry: Artisan cheese board with local honey

restaurants.name: Marie-Clarisse
restaurants.description: Intimate seafood restaurant overlooking the St. Lawrence River with fresh daily catches. Sophisticated yet unpretentious dining experience highlighting Quebec's maritime heritage.
restaurants.mustTry: Whole grilled fish with herb butter

restaurants.name: Chez Muffy
restaurants.description: Beloved diner serving traditional Quebec breakfast and brunch dishes all day long. Famous for thick-cut french toast and authentic maple syrup preparations.

restaurants.name: Hydrant Espresso
restaurants.description: Trendy specialty coffee roastery in Saint-Roch with locally roasted beans and pastries. Minimalist design attracts creative locals and tourists seeking great caffeine.

restaurants.name: La Fenouillère
restaurants.description: Michelin-listed restaurant offering innovative French-Quebec fusion cuisine in an intimate setting. Chef-driven tasting menus showcase seasonal ingredients and artistic plating.

restaurants.name: Charlevoix Brewpub
restaurants.description: Craft brewery and gastropub serving locally brewed beers paired with hearty Quebecois pub fare. Rustic interior with exposed stone creates warm, welcoming atmosphere.
restaurants.mustTry: Quebec tourtière with house amber ale

restaurants.name: Gourmet Burger Truck
restaurants.description: Food truck phenomenon in Old Quebec serving gourmet burgers with local beef and creative toppings. Perfect quick lunch option while exploring historic streets.
restaurants.mustTry: Quebec cheddar burger with maple aioli

restaurants.name: L'Eau à la Bouche
restaurants.description: Contemporary bistro focusing on locally sourced ingredients and seasonal menus. Friendly service and relaxed ambiance make it perfect for casual dining.
restaurants.mustTry: Salmon with dill and local vegetables

activities.name: Explore Old Quebec (Vieux-Québec)
activities.description: Wander the UNESCO World Heritage district with cobblestone streets, historic architecture, and charming shops. Visit iconic sites like the Château Frontenac and Cathedral-Basilica.

activities.name: Montmorency Falls Hike
activities.description: Scenic waterfall just 15 minutes north of the city offering trails with stunning views of the St. Lawrence River. Challenge yourself with 487 steps or enjoy easier riverside paths.

activities.name: Île d'Orléans Cycling Tour
activities.description: Pedal through this charming island with farms, artisan shops, and historic villages. Rent bikes to explore 47 kilometers of scenic routes with river views.

activities.name: Musée de la Civilisation
activities.description: World-class museum exploring Quebec's history, culture, and civilization through interactive exhibits. Features rotating contemporary art and traveling exhibitions.

activities.name: Terrasse Dufferin Stroll
activities.description: Iconic wooden boardwalk along the St. Lawrence River offering panoramic views and street performers. Perfect for sunset walks, people-watching, and photography.

activities.name: Quebec Winter Carnival (Seasonal)
activities.description: North America's largest winter festival featuring ice sculptures, dog sledding races, and traditional snow activities. Held in February with parades and live entertainment.

activities.name: Basilica-Cathedral of Quebec
activities.description: Stunning Gothic Revival cathedral with intricate architectural details and sacred art collections. Active place of worship since 1647 with guided tours available.

activities.name: Kayaking the St. Lawrence River
activities.description: Paddle along the scenic river with views of Old Quebec and surrounding landscapes. Guided tours accommodate all skill levels from beginner to advanced.

activities.name: Artisan Markets & Galleries
activities.description: Browse local artist studios, craft shops, and weekend markets throughout Saint-Roch neighborhood. Discover unique handmade goods, art, and local creations.

activities.name: Montmorency Park Picnic
activities.description: Pack local cheese and wine for a leisurely picnic with waterfall views. Peaceful grassy areas perfect for relaxation and enjoying Quebec's natural beauty.

activities.name: Ghost Tour of Old Quebec
activities.description: Evening walking tour exploring the haunted history and ghost stories of historic Old Quebec. Guides share legends and historical tales through atmospheric streets.

activities.name: Rue Saint-Jean Shopping & Dining
activities.description: Main pedestrian street lined with independent boutiques, cafes, restaurants, and live music venues. Vibrant hub for shopping, eating, and experiencing local culture.

spots.name: Château Frontenac
spots.description: Iconic turretted hotel dominating the Quebec City skyline with picturesque views from multiple angles including Terrasse Dufferin.
spots.bestTime: Golden hour for warm light on stone facade; winter for snow-covered landscape

spots.name: Montmorency Falls
spots.description: Powerful 83-meter waterfall cascading into the St. Lawrence River with verdant cliff surroundings and multiple viewpoint angles.
spots.bestTime: Spring during snowmelt for maximum water flow; overcast days eliminate harsh shadows

spots.name: Terrasse Dufferin at Sunset
spots.description: Wooden boardwalk stretching along the river with sweeping vistas, street performers, and warm light bathing historic architecture.
spots.bestTime: 30 minutes before sunset through dusk for optimal golden and blue light

spots.name: Rue du Petit-Champlain
spots.description: Charming historic narrow street lined with colorful buildings, old storefronts, and cobblestones creating quintessential European atmosphere.
spots.bestTime: Early morning before crowds; afternoon light reflects off stone facades

spots.name: Île d'Orléans Rural Landscape
spots.description: Rolling farmland with traditional houses, apple orchards, and river views creating pastoral Quebec countryside scenery.
spots.bestTime: Early fall with harvest scenes; spring with blooming orchards

spots.name: Quebec City Cityscape from Lévis
spots.description: Across-river perspective showcasing the entire Old Quebec skyline with St. Lawrence River in foreground reflecting light.
spots.bestTime: Sunset for backlit cityscape; overcast days for even exposure across water and buildings

spots.name: Cathedral-Basilica Interior
spots.description: Ornate Gothic Revival interior with intricate wooden ceilings, stained glass, and candlelit sacred artworks.
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon when side light illuminates stained glass; avoid flash photography

spots.name: Saint-Roch Street Art & Murals
spots.description: Vibrant neighborhood featuring colorful murals, street art installations, and creative urban expressions on historic buildings.
spots.bestTime: Bright midday sun for saturated colors; blue hour for dramatic contrast

spots.name: St. Lawrence River Frozen (Winter)
spots.description: Dramatic winter landscape showing ice formations along the riverbank with snow-covered landscape and clear skies.
spots.bestTime: Early morning light across frozen surface; clear days for detail and texture

spots.name: Market Square (Place Royale)
spots.description: Historic plaza surrounded by 17th-century architecture featuring the bust of King Louis XIV and atmospheric street-level perspectives.
spots.bestTime: Morning light; golden hour for warm tones on stone buildings

lensRecommendations: 24-70mm f/2.8 for architectural detail and street scenes in varied lighting conditions
70-200mm f/2.8 for compressed river landscapes and distant cityscape perspectives
16-35mm f/2.8 for expansive waterfall and landscape compositions, especially at Montmorency Falls
50mm f/1.4 for intimate street portraiture and moody golden hour atmospheric shots
photography.goldenHourNotes: Quebec City's golden hour is particularly magical from 7-8 AM and 5-6 PM, with low-angled sun illuminating historic stone facades in warm amber tones. The Château Frontenac and riverside buildings glow beautifully during these periods. Winter extends golden hour with lower sun trajectories, while summer's extended daylight creates extended shooting windows ideal for photographers.

weather.seasonality: Winter (December-February) brings severe snow and cold perfect for winter activities but challenging travel. Spring (March-May) offers mild weather with blooming scenery. Summer (June-August) is warm and ideal for outdoor activities. Fall (September-November) showcases stunning foliage but increasingly cold and rainy.
weather.summary: Quebec City experiences four distinct seasons with cold, snowy winters averaging -9°C and pleasant summers around 23°C. Late May through September provides the best weather for visiting, while winter transforms the city into a magical snowy landscape ideal for seasonal activities and festivals.

hotels.name: Auberge Saint-Antoine
hotels.description: Historic hotel in Old Quebec with river views, on-site archaeology museum, and excellent restaurant Panache featuring contemporary French cuisine.

hotels.name: Le Capitole Hôtel
hotels.description: Converted historic theater building offering affordable lodging with character, located in vibrant Saint-Roch neighborhood near galleries and restaurants.

hotels.name: Fairmont Le Château Frontenac
hotels.description: Iconic castle-like luxury hotel dominating the skyline with panoramic river views, spa facilities, fine dining, and impeccable service in the heart of Old Quebec.
